## Findings 1/3 — reproduced amplification + five-measure comparison (AC1, AC2)

**Mechanism (code-grounded).** `compact_plan.needs_folding(foldable, has_snap, threshold)` returns `foldable > threshold` (default `compact.threshold = 10`, see `_commands/compact.py`). On each fold, `compact_plan.build_snapshot_event` embeds the **complete** `compiled_state` — whose `state["comments"]` list (`reducer/_state.py`, `reducer/_processors.process_comment`) grows linearly — and `compact_txn._retire_folded_sources` renames the folded sources **and the prior SNAPSHOT** to `*.retired` (I1 append-only, never deleted). So for a state of size S that keeps growing, every ~T events writes a fresh full-state snapshot of size ~S and retains all prior ones: retained snapshot bytes are Θ(S·(N/T)) = **Θ(N²)**.

**Measured** (`python bench_snapshot_cadence.py`, body=1800 B, hot-edge=5), retired-snapshot bytes:

| events | A fixed T=10 (control) | B geometric r=1.0 | C byte-cost α=0.5 | C byte-cost α=1.0 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1,000 | 81,516,039 | 1,166,686 | 2,988,007 | 1,076,041 |
| 4,000 | 1,337,518,615 | 4,719,278 | 14,198,214 | 4,117,838 |
| 8,000 | 5,357,939,635 | 9,456,994 | 30,783,337 | 15,581,244 |

Full five measures @ N=8,000:

| policy | snaps | retired-snap B | active-snap B | source B | max-replay events | end-replay events |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A fixed T=10 (control) | 726 | 5,357,939,635 | 14,781,242 | 15,736,000 | 16 | 14 |
| B geometric r=1.0 | 10 | 9,456,994 | 9,476,276 | 15,736,000 | 2,880 | 2,880 |
| C byte-cost α=0.5 | 18 | 30,783,337 | 14,518,400 | 15,736,000 | 2,515 | 156 |
| C byte-cost α=1.0 | 11 | 15,581,244 | 14,686,841 | 15,736,000 | 3,852 | 65 |

**Amplification confirmed superlinear for the control**: 1k→4k events (4×) → 16.4× retired bytes; 4k→8k (2×) → 4.0× retired bytes — i.e. **Θ(N²)**. Both candidates are **Θ(N)**. Source-event bytes are identical across policies (all sources retained under I1; cadence changes only the snapshot term). Snapshot count: control Θ(N/T)=726; candidates Θ(log N)=10–18.

**Amplification factor** (retired-snapshot bytes ÷ final active-snapshot bytes) @ N=8,000: control **362×** (and unboundedly growing ∝ N/T); geometric **1.0×**; byte-cost α=0.5 **2.12× (≈1/α)**; byte-cost α=1.0 **1.06× (≈1/α)**. This is the design knob: sum of geometrically-spaced snapshot bases ≈ S_final · (1+α)/α, so retained-snapshot bytes ≈ **(1/α)·S_final**, linear and tunable.
